summary: The admitted Sokoban case reaches trap.c:sokoban_guilt() from read.c:seffect_earth(); the missing helper caused the final conduct-line mismatch. Independent recipes now reach its other active callers in zap.c, hack.c, and steed.c and match the patched C recordings. The steed recipe initially exposed a missing supporting caller: polyself.c:polymon() must invoke dismount_steed(DISMOUNT_POLY) after the transformed hero can no longer ride. Once wired, the existing landing_spot() path matched C without a landing_spot implementation change; this task claims only the whole trap.c:sokoban_guilt source unit.

source.branch: The whole trap.c:sokoban_guilt() checks the current-level Sokoban flag. If set, it increments u.uconduct.sokocheat and calls change_luck(-1). It emits no message and consumes no RNG. Its result is void. JavaScript implements this helper in js/trap.js and wires each active caller.

callers.source: read.c:seffect_earth():1951 calls sokoban_guilt() after earth scroll boulder effects; admitted v46 case v46-sokoban-earth-guilt-branch-entry-attempt24 reaches the helper and the later insight.c:show_conduct() display.
zap.c:poly_obj():1711 calls sokoban_guilt() when polymorph changes a boulder in Sokoban.
zap.c:fracture_rock():5556 calls sokoban_guilt() for its boulder/rock fracture result.
hack.c:cannot_push():299,307 calls sokoban_guilt() on both relevant refusal branches.
hack.c:moverock_core():398,403 calls sokoban_guilt() on its two boulder movement branches.

steed.c:dismount_steed():767 calls sokoban_guilt() after teleds() lands the hero on a boulder. Supporting caller wiring is polyself.c:polymon():964 -> js/polyself.js:polymon(), which invokes dismount_steed(DISMOUNT_POLY) when can_ride() rejects the transformed hero. That route uses the existing landing_spot() implementation; landing_spot() is not claimed as completed by this task.

dependencies: attrib.c:change_luck(-1) is an existing JavaScript owner in js/moveloop_preamble.js; C discards its void result.

selectionReason: Selected candidate 6, the first unreserved item in saved combined queue SHA-256 9d2425b60017f469943e7c22789e06736445e2c603c966cfcde87f3250e5d528 at accepted Main 696981041adb7876b92090fe5486dc9ca68af575. B owns the random-swamp case; C owns prayer, crystal-ball, and succubus; earlier A2 deliveries own troll-meal and lit-candle. This Sokoban guilt case is independent from those reservations.
evidence: The immutable v46 manifest identifies read.c:seffect_earth() and trap.c:sokoban_guilt(). At segment 0 step 119/key newline, the accepted baseline matches 6,674 RNG calls and 120/121 screens; JavaScript lacks the changed Sokoban conduct count, so the final conduct line differs.

nethack-c/upstream/src/trap.c:7039-7054 defines the whole helper. Its only effects are guarded by the current-level Sokoban flag: increment u.uconduct.sokocheat and call change_luck(-1). The function has no RNG, message, or screen output.

Active direct callers are read.c:seffect_earth():1951, zap.c:poly_obj():1711, zap.c:fracture_rock():5556, hack.c:cannot_push():299/307, hack.c:moverock_core():398/403, and steed.c:dismount_steed():767. Their JavaScript caller wiring invokes js/trap.js:sokoban_guilt().

The steed recording initially diverged before reaching Sokoban guilt because JS polyself.js:polymon() recorded note_unported instead of following polyself.c:polymon():964 into dismount_steed(DISMOUNT_POLY). The supporting caller was wired and the branch added to the existing dismount implementation. The resulting recipe strictly matches C through 5,744 RNG calls, 106 screens, and 106 cursors. It reaches the existing steed.c:landing_spot() and then Sokoban guilt; landing_spot() itself was not changed or claimed complete.

Independent trap.c recipes and recordings exercise poly_obj, fracture_rock, moverock_core, cannot_push, and the steed dismount route. The admitted v46 case provides the seffect_earth route. Together they cover all active direct helper callers listed above.
